scope: Entire current MnemoCode checkout, including dirty/untracked source, core representations/masking/recovery, coin evidence, SSKR Rust/WASM, CLI, cards/QR, tests/startup checks, packaging, workflows and documentation. No sibling repository mutation or browser execution.

coverageLedger.evidence: Age diagnostic redaction: SEC003; explicit secret getters and immutable strings remain host responsibilities.

coverageLedger.title: Process sandbox and transport
coverageLedger.evidence: Node permissions, OS hardening/refusals and startup reporting traced; enforcement evidence is limited to executed Linux checks.

coverageLedger.title: Network egress
coverageLedger.evidence: No first-party runtime network request path found; library consumers must supply isolation. Platform gaps remain explicit.

coverageLedger.title: Randomness, encryption and authentication
coverageLedger.evidence: CSPRNG/age authentication and fixed scrypt admission traced; SEC003 diagnostic failure reproduced.

coverageLedger.title: Lifecycle and exceptional paths
coverageLedger.evidence: Wiping scopes, raw input, staging and search publication reviewed. Inner PDF buffers, immutable strings and dependency erasure remain hardening limits.

coverageLedger.title: Browser and sensitive APIs
coverageLedger.evidence: Host-neutral library reviewed. DOM/storage/CSP are outside this checkout; the consuming browser host has the BLD001 parity gate.

coverageLedger.title: Availability bounds
coverageLedger.evidence: Small actual PNG-decoder probes confirm SEC001/SEC002; search/share/input admission reviewed without exhaustion workloads.

coverageLedger.title: BIP39, representations and masking
coverageLedger.evidence: All lengths/forms/modes reviewed; FUN001 reproduced. Independent-oracle execution is recorded separately.

coverageLedger.title: HD derivation and coins

findings.title: Duplicate PNG headers bypass the dimension admission limit
findings.reproduction: Run security-probes.mjs: first IHDR 1x1, second IHDR 4097x1, valid CRCs and 4098 zero scanline bytes; actual production QR reader delegates to the real PNG decoder.
findings.expected: Admission must bound the dimensions used by the decoder before allocation.
findings.observed: The first header passes; real PNG.sync.read returns width 4097 and QR scanning runs before the no-readable-QR refusal.
findings.impact: Crafted operator-selected local images bypass a resource limit. No OOM, successful QR extraction or larger allocation was attempted.
findings.recommendedFix: Reject duplicate/invalid IHDR structure and bound authoritative decoder dimensions before allocation.
findings.requiredVerification: Include small duplicate-header fixtures, normal valid PNG controls, pixel/side limits and rejection-before-decoding assertions.

findings.title: Interlaced PNG decompression is not bounded by admitted dimensions
findings.reproduction: Run security-probes.mjs with a valid-CRC 1x1 RGBA interlaced PNG whose IDAT expands to 65536 zero bytes; do not enlarge the fixture.
findings.expected: Inflation must have a bound derived from accepted PNG layout and reject surplus data.
findings.observed: Real zlib.inflateSync produces 65536 bytes without maxOutputLength before malformed-image refusal.
findings.impact: Highly compressible local inputs can consume excess memory/CPU before rejection. The 16 MiB input limit still holds; no exhaustion or crash was attempted.
findings.recommendedFix: Bound interlaced inflation with the accepted Adam7/bit-depth/color layout, or explicitly reject unsupported interlacing before decoding.
findings.requiredVerification: Tiny excessive-inflation negative control, valid interlaced/noninterlaced controls, and finite output-bound assertions.

findings.title: Declared word counts discard Color Unicode recovery marks
findings.reproduction: Run core-probes.mjs with the direct-12 Color Unicode vector, a late ? and words:12; compare spaced hexadecimal and Private Use symbols with the no-count controls.
findings.expected: Known record format must govern cropping, and genuine unknown-code marks must survive while trailing decoys are excluded.
findings.observed: Both late hexadecimal and symbol marks disappear from marked detection; named hexadecimal missingCodes admission still works.
findings.impact: Supported damaged backups can be routed to complete-input decoding or refused. Omitting the declared word count is a workaround; no wrong wallet was published.
findings.recommendedFix: Use the record/named form for mark detection and preserve ? placeholders during Color Unicode prefix extraction.
findings.requiredVerification: Every BIP39 length, raw/MNC1, joined/apart hex and symbols, leading genuine marks and trailing decoys.

findings.title: Marked SSKR share repair rejects trailing card decoys
findings.reproduction: Run core-probes.mjs: replace #1F9121 in public sskrSetVector.colors[0] with ?, then append #000000. Compare marked-only and complete-plus-decoy controls.
findings.expected: Repair must use the recorded share prefix consistently with complete reading and documented trailing decoys.
findings.observed: The marked-only share repairs to the canonical UR and the complete share accepts the decoy; their combination is refused.
findings.impact: Handwritten share-card recovery fails for an otherwise repairable input. Removing trailing decoys is a workaround; no invalid share or cryptographic weakness was demonstrated.
findings.recommendedFix: Select/crop candidate share prefixes from validated metadata while preserving ambiguity/checksum checks.
findings.requiredVerification: Known length, marked length/header cases, trailing decoys in supported forms and joint recovery with another intact share.

findings.title: Candidate-list encoding silently narrows non-byte entropy
findings.reproduction: Run core-probes.mjs: encode one record with new Uint16Array(16).fill(256), then decode the list; valid Uint8Array control is included.
findings.expected: Reject a runtime entropy type that does not represent BIP39 bytes.
findings.observed: A valid list with sixteen zero bytes is emitted and its CRC is computed over those unintended bytes.
findings.impact: Public JavaScript callers can serialize a different candidate from their supplied data. Normal CLI searches supply correct Uint8Array values; no CLI corruption is claimed.
findings.recommendedFix: Validate byte-array type and byte length centrally before constructing any list data.
findings.requiredVerification: Uint8Array/Buffer/subarray controls; Uint16Array, ordinary out-of-range arrays, holes, null and mixed record refusals.

findings.title: Re-encoding confirmation does not own the confirmed phrase
findings.reproduction: Run core-probes.mjs: deferred wallet check receives public phrase P; change result.recoveredMnemonic to public Q before resolving matched:true.
findings.expected: A confirmed result must remain bound to the phrase actually checked, or refuse after a change.
findings.observed: The wallet callback checked P, but confirmedPhrase returns Q.
findings.impact: Public API state consistency is violated. TypeScript readonly and current CLI behavior are counterevidence; the trusted caller already has plaintext. This is not a newly crossed security authority boundary.
findings.recommendedFix: Own an immutable decoded snapshot or return safe immutable/copy views; bind confirmation to that exact snapshot.
findings.requiredVerification: Mutation during/after wallet or personal confirmation; arrays/result ownership; CLI output preservation and mismatched-wallet refusal.

findings.title: Browser integration lacks the unreleased re-encoding feature
findings.reproduction: Inspect the host owner's reported vendor mapping and feature composition, then trace the package exports and CLI/self-test feature. Targeted read-only sibling inspection independently confirms the absence.
findings.expected: Every CLI feature must have its host-neutral library, browser integration, checks and handover completed before release.
findings.observed: The re-encoding workflow, module and startup checks are absent from the browser vendor mapping/wrapper/UI. Thirteen mapped sources also drift from this MnemoCode snapshot.
findings.impact: The mandatory browser parity gate is unmet. Manual Decode then Encode remains available; no incorrect output from existing browser features is claimed.
findings.recommendedFix: Coordinate a precise source-bound handover and browser implementation with the Wallet tools owner; do not edit that owner's repository here.
findings.requiredVerification: Vendor integrity, both browser editions' feature composition/startup checks, and terminal/browser regression acceptance on the same source revision.

findings.title: Malformed age identities are copied into diagnostic errors
findings.reproduction: Run security-probes.mjs using the published age identity and encrypted file in vectors/candidates-v1.json; change only its final checksum character.
findings.expected: Private identity material must be absent from error messages and retained causes.
findings.observed: addIdentity throws a checksum error containing the complete supplied identity. Its private payload is unchanged by the checksum typo.
findings.impact: Secret-bearing diagnostics are confirmed; no external logging sink, unauthorized observer or CLI decryption route was demonstrated. Low severity reflects that bounded evidence, while release is blocked by the secret-redaction policy.
findings.recommendedFix: Catch and sanitize identity parsing failures without retaining a secret-bearing cause or interpolated original diagnostic.
findings.requiredVerification: Assert absence of full key and key payload in message/cause/inspection for malformed identities, with valid-key and wrong-key controls.

findings.title: Separate export destinations receive different decorative decoy plans
findings.reproduction: Run the audit-only export-probe.ts through its isolated Vitest configuration. Exercise runEncode with three destinations, deterministic randomness, a passive saver and a lightweight sheet shaper.
findings.expected: The documented one-content export plan should give the same complete card collection to PDF, page images and separate cards.
findings.observed: The first eight real backup codes match, but the three per-destination decoy collections differ. No image or PDF was rendered by the probe.
findings.impact: This is a bounded export consistency defect; QR payload, real backup codes and cached identity details remain the same. The initial frozen-renderer mutation mistake is preserved separately.
findings.recommendedFix: Plan and retain one card collection before iterating save destinations; keep platform and saving adapters separate.
findings.requiredVerification: Production dispatcher regression comparing complete planned collections across all destinations, plus representative rendering/QR checks.

findings.title: Heir instructions overgeneralize wrong-date behavior
findings.reproduction: Run document-probes.mjs: text-only instructions for seedshift-legacy promise no wrong-date error; the existing public legacy fixture decoded with 24-09-2026 fails its checksum.
findings.expected: Instructions must distinguish current Seedshift, legacy modes and direct encoding and avoid guaranteeing an empty wallet.
findings.observed: Printed/public heir guidance promises no error for a wrong date and an empty wallet, while legacy mode can reject that date. README/help already distinguish modes.
findings.impact: Recovery guidance can confuse an heir. Not every wrong legacy date fails; recovery checks are still available.
findings.recommendedFix: Describe the actual behavior by masking mode and explain that a valid phrase or an empty-looking wallet does not establish ownership.
findings.requiredVerification: Text assertions for every supported mode and public wrong-date checksum controls; representative heir-sheet layout.

findings.title: Help text duplicates centrally owned recovery limits
findings.reproduction: Run document-probes.mjs and inspect help source: literals 16,777,216 and 2,048 appear in prose despite exported owners.
findings.expected: Workspace DRY rules require each meaningful limit to have one source and help to format the library values.
findings.observed: The help literals currently agree with the library but are independently maintained. The token copy detector does not detect this semantic duplication.
findings.impact: No current incorrect limit or security failure was shown; future documentation drift and explicit architecture-rule noncompliance are the bounded impact.
findings.recommendedFix: Interpolate MAX_SEARCH_COMBINATIONS and MAX_SHOWN_CANDIDATES with the existing formatting convention.
findings.requiredVerification: Help output checks bound to the exported values, plus the existing type/copy gate.

findings.title: Release tag recipe omits the required UTC environment
findings.reproduction: Inspect the documented git tag -s v0.1.0 recipe without executing it.
findings.expected: Every command that writes a commit/tag date must run with TZ=UTC under the workspace privacy rule.
findings.observed: The published signed-tag recipe omits TZ=UTC.
findings.impact: A maintainer using a non-UTC environment could publish a local time offset. No tag was created or shown to be incorrectly dated.
findings.recommendedFix: Prefix the documented signing/tag command with TZ=UTC and audit all date-writing examples.
findings.requiredVerification: Static recipe check and inspection of any future tag's dates/signature; no tag creation is needed for this fix.

findings.title: The package ships an audit index without its linked records
findings.reproduction: Run npm pack --dry-run --json --ignore-scripts and inspect the 540-path manifest. Compare the audit index's report/harness links with its entries.
findings.expected: Documentation shipped in an archive must have usable evidence links or explicitly link to the repository copies.
findings.observed: docs/audits/README.md is included; zero numbered AUD-* records or harnesses are included. The package includes dist/core/re-encoding.js and the ordinary public vectors.
findings.impact: Local evidence navigation is broken in the prospective archive. Repository links remain valid and private:true limits npm publication reach; no package was published.
findings.recommendedFix: Either include the public report/harness files while continuing to exclude evidence, or make the distributed index link explicitly to repository copies.
findings.requiredVerification: Dry-run file-list assertions for index link targets and absence of every *-evidence file; no publication required.

remediation.evidence: PngAdmission validates the complete chunk stream and rejects duplicate headers before decoding.
Exact channel/depth/Adam7 budgets bound pre-inflation before pixels; odd, packed and 16-bit valid controls decode.
Declared length and record-owned format preserve Color Unicode marks in every supported spelling and phrase length.
Repair uses supported share prefixes and complete valid decoys, retains checks, and refuses incomplete capped readings.
Entropy fields are read once; intrinsic element kind and storage length reject spoofed prototypes/properties, accept genuine cross-realm bytes, and own/wipe copies before passphrases.
ReEncoding owns and freezes decoded arrays/dates and retains exactly the phrase confirmed by the person or wallet.

Browser ReEncoding uses the shared owner and normal Encode handoff; all 60 obligations are mapped, 175 vendored files match, and selected regressions/default HTML gates passed. Actual-browser acceptance is not asserted.
Malformed age identity diagnostics have fixed text and no retained cause; public valid/wrong-key controls pass.
One successful card plan is shared by all destinations in one run; retries, rename and skip preserve it.
Mode-owned advice distinguishes legacy checksum errors and makes no empty-wallet/unique-date guarantee; UR instructions no longer promise unsupported Bytewords cards.
Help reads the recovery owners' constants instead of repeating numeric limits.
The signed tag recipe explicitly uses TZ=UTC; no tag was made.
The package includes numbered reports and all public harness files, including mts and the nested Docker shim; evidence stays excluded.

recommendations: Add bounded negative tests specified for every confirmed finding; place hostile-input admission tests in unit/CLI regressions, not slow startup checks.
Startup already composes exact known answers with refusal/fault-injection controls. Keep it fast; startup cannot replace hostile-input regression tests or release-level vectors/rendering.
Optional hardening: reject operations on disposed candidate lists, release passphrase references, wipe intermediate PDF buffers and clarify dependency/WASM erasure limits.
Cooperative cancellation may emit one final progress callback after an unmatched wallet answer; no match or successful result is published. An earlier guard is an optional UI improvement.
Threshold-one imported SSKR is intentionally supported; a checked result does not add cryptographic authentication. Improve wording rather than inventing a threshold prohibition.
Consolidate repeated RGB maxima if it simplifies ownership; clarify roadmap bullets for features already present in TypeScript; pin the upstream SSKR vector to a full revision/hash.
Preserve the owner's deferred G1-001 and S123/S120 decisions. No risk acceptance is inferred.
limitations: Open release-blocking findings establish FAIL independently of incomplete execution gates. No critical/high finding or direct secret compromise was demonstrated.
Two complete-gallery tests excluded by the owner; no full-gallery script run. Original full-suite and batch timeouts and the initial failed export harness attempt remain in the evidence.
Current dirty-source Windows/macOS and real browser acceptance are absent. HEAD Windows PTY failed both remote workflows; those traces do not establish the cause or behavior of the dirty source.

No fresh uncached canonical Docker/WASM comparison, clean dependency reinstall or signed release provenance was performed. The native pre-tag procedure defers verify:sskr to the tag workflow; installed-pin/integrity matches are narrower evidence.

The guard requires 4 GiB available before starting, stops below 3 GiB, caps the Node heap at 768 MiB and runs files one at a time. Deadlines apply only to command execution; test assertions/timeouts and cryptographic parameters were not relaxed.
Linux system self-test reporting is not proof that every OS mitigation held. Core-limit readback, other platforms, dependency erasure and host storage/DOM controls remain limited evidence.

Auditing is not independent certification, proof of defect absence or publication. No production/test/fixture/dependency/workflow changes, commit, push, tag, release upload, signing or paid CI dispatch occurred.
